prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider._initialize() loads stored tokens but never recomputes `token_expiry_time` from the token's `expires_in`, so `is_token_valid()` treats an already-expired stored token as valid after a process restart, causing the proactive refresh path to be skipped and forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (3 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the root cause directly at the source (`_initialize`) with the minimal change — guarding on `expires_in is not None` before calling `update_token_expiry`, mirroring the existing write-path behavior in `set_tokens` — and ships a regression test via the new `expired_tokens` fixture. #3251 makes the identical `_initialize` fix but bundles it with an unrelated oauth_metadata-persistence feature implemented via untyped `getattr` duck-typing rather than a declared interface. #2875 doesn't touch `_initialize` at all; it patches around the same root cause reactively inside the 401-handling branch of `async_auth_flow`, leaving `is_token_valid()` itself still returning an incorrect result for any other caller.

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug: concurrent requests with duplicate JSON-RPC request ids overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug: concurrent requests with duplicate JSON-RPC request ids overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids like int 1 and string "1" into the same key (false-positive 409, or cross-wiring) and can still collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel if a string id equals "_GET_stream". #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key` helper that prefixes by type (`i:`/`s:`) to keep int/string ids distinct and prevent collision with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing edge cases #3063's simpler `in` check misses while solving the identical underlying duplicate-id problem.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: All three fix the same root cause: pickling an MCPError subclass (surfaced via UrlElicitationRequiredError, issue #2431) fails because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args (code, message, data) doesn't match subclass __init__ signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising TypeError on unpickle and/or losing the original error payload. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: All three fix the same root cause: pickling an MCPError subclass (surfaced via UrlElicitationRequiredError, issue #2431) fails because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args (code, message, data) doesn't match subclass __init__ signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising TypeError on unpickle and/or losing the original error payload. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restore, so it covers every subclass generically without invoking any subclass constructor; its test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError, showing the fix generalizes beyond the one subclass originally reported. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-standard constructor remains broken. 2478 also fixes it via a base-class helper (_restore_mcp_error) but hardcodes a branch keyed on 'exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' and reconstructs through from_error/from_error_data classmethods, so each new subclass with an incompatible constructor needs a future code change to this dispatch — less generic than 3262's constructor-free __new__/__dict__ approach.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restore, so it covers every subclass generically without invoking any subclass constructor; its test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError, showing the fix generalizes beyond the one subclass originally reported. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-standard constructor remains broken. 2478 also fixes it via a base-class helper (_restore_mcp_error) but hardcodes a branch keyed on 'exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' and reconstructs through from_error/from_error_data classmethods, so each new subclass with an incompatible constructor needs a future code change to this dispatch — less generic than 3262's constructor-free __new__/__dict__ approach.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restore, so it covers every subclass generically without invoking any subclass constructor; its test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError, showing the fix generalizes beyond the one subclass originally reported. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-standard constructor remains broken. 2478 also fixes it via a base-class helper (_restore_mcp_error) but hardcodes a branch keyed on 'exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' and reconstructs through from_error/from_error_data classmethods, so each new subclass with an incompatible constructor needs a future code change to this dispatch — less generic than 3262's constructor-free __new__/__dict__ approach.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids like int 1 and string "1" into the same key (false-positive 409, or cross-wiring) and can still collide with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel if a string id equals "_GET_stream". #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key` helper that prefixes by type (`i:`/`s:`) to keep int/string ids distinct and prevent collision with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing edge cases #3063's simpler `in` check misses while solving the identical underlying duplicate-id problem.
